findings.summary: rounds.md's rendering rule now claims the title removals and isolates protect only text that bypasses the forms, which is false because dir=auto and FSI/PDI still isolate RTL text and the allowed LRM/RLM/ALM marks; the SECURITY-SPEC bullet similarly drops that rationale.

Decisions 2 and 3 are not met: no residual is recorded in SECURITY-SPEC for unrefused zero-width characters and joiners (deferred to #22) or for look-alike labels that the allowed direction marks can produce.

SECURITY-SPEC.md, the home for controls and residual gaps, is not updated: the new input refusal is not listed, and decisions 2 and 3's residuals (zero-width and joiner characters not refused, deferred to #22; look-alike labels from the allowed marks) are not recorded in any reviewed file.

The rendering rule in rounds.md now claims each rules criterion tests direction marks in rendered text, but the RND-1.7, RND-2.8 and RND-6.5 rendering tests (test_rendering.py, test_record_rendering.py, test_close.py) use no marks, so the spec claims tests that do not exist.
The refusal and acceptance tests only exercise the new-criterion and new-case routes, so the criterion and case edit inputs that RND-2.8 now promises to refuse are never sent a direction control.

RND-1.7, RND-2.8, RND-3.6 and RND-5.8 now claim their tests include the text-direction refusal, but the new tests carry no criterion marks (their docstring says so), so the criteria's claims are not backed by tests marked with their IDs.

Rule 5 now states the checks run strictly in the order length, null, direction, visibility, but Django runs the length and null-character checks together, so text that is too long and contains a null gets both messages; the rule also restates the per-field length message that the criteria already hold.

The edited rendering rule says every rules criterion tests rendering of typed-in direction marks, but only RND-1.7 has such a test (built via make_round, not typed), so RND-2.8, RND-3.6 and RND-5.8 lack the promised rendering tests.

Decisions 2 and 3 are not recorded as residuals: SECURITY-SPEC has no accepted residual for unrefused zero-width/joiner characters (with #22) or for look-alike text the allowed direction marks can produce, and rule 5 only says other invisible characters are not refused.

The edited rendering rule in rounds.md says each criterion tests how the direction marks render and no longer lists the bidi controls, but no test renders LRM/RLM/ALM and the existing rendering tests still use RLO/LRI.
`HEX = lambda ...` in test_direction_controls.py violates Ruff's default E731 rule, so the required `ruff check .` verification would fail.

The rendering rule in rounds.md now says each rules criterion tests direction-mark rendering, but only RND-5.8 has such tests; RND-1.7, RND-2.8 and RND-3.6 rendering tests use only U+202E, U+200B and U+2066.

The allowed-character test covers only LRM, RLM, ALM and ZWSP, so a regression that refused joiners (U+200C/U+200D), right-to-left script letters or the characters next to the refused ranges (U+2029, U+202F, U+2065, U+206A) would not fail any test.

The RND-3.6 and RND-5.8 rendering tests (round-page build labels, retest and sign-in messages) were switched from bidi controls to direction marks without adding the saved-text bidi-control tests that the new rendering-rule sentence requires, so only the Closed page still covers saved bidi labels.

The rendering rule now says each requirement's rules criterion tests direction-mark characters, but the RND-1, RND-2 and RND-6.5 rendering tests (test_rendering, test_record_rendering, test_close) were not extended with LRM/RLM/ALM.

The new SECURITY-SPEC residual explains accepting look-alike labels by saying mark-inserted labels equal the plain label, which means they would be refused as duplicates; the real residual is RLM/ALM reordering neutral characters so a different label, title or case looks like another.

SECURITY-SPEC records the 'stored text not cleaned / Draft item uneditable with nothing visible to remove' residual as accepted by the human on 2026-10-27 (#68), but the human's decisions accepted only the zero-width and direction-mark look-alike residuals, so this misstates an approval.

The build-label rendering tests (test_publish.py:641, test_retest.py:672, test_messages.py:172) were switched to allowed marks, and no test writes a build label with real bidi controls into the database, so RND-3.6's rendering coverage of bidi controls in already-saved labels is gone, despite rounds.md now saying tests put controls in stored text directly.
TECHNICAL-SPEC.md 'Text fields' still says the shared round text field applies only the visibility check, length limits and null-character validator, omitting the new text-direction control refusal.
SECURITY-SPEC records a new residual as 'not yet seen by the human' and points to a plan file that is absent, instead of stating it fully in its home and resolving its acceptance before merge.

The view-level text-direction refusal tests cover only criterion text and case title (not steps or expected result, unlike the adjacent null-character test over all FIELDS) and only round creation (not retitling), so not every round text input is tested to refuse the controls.
The retest storage-failure test mocks the whole services.retest, so it never checks that a Build written before a failing BuildCase insert is rolled back, unlike the publish test.

The new SECURITY-SPEC residual attributes to the human's RND-5 decision an acceptance of an IntegrityError log record carrying the label's key, which the human never gave and which contradicts decision 6, so it records an approval that was not given.

rounds.md RND-5 says a round closed while its form is being filled out shows invalid-field messages at 200, contradicting its own preceding sentence, the view's state check before the form, and the User Guide; only a close committing mid-request behaves that way.

Result stores no submission timestamp although RND-4.1 requires each submitted result's submission time, and the edited RND-4 intro now says RES-2 defines those fields, so the specs contradict each other and immutable submitted rows can never gain a true time.
SECURITY-SPEC drops the earlier 'RES must cap results' requirement and records an ~18 GiB/day result-storage gap as open and not accepted, so a human must accept it or ask for a cap before merge.

SECURITY-SPEC records result storage (~4.8 billion characters, ~18 GiB a day, about 11x the accepted gap) as an open risk awaiting a human decision, so it needs explicit acceptance or a result cap before merge, given the earlier 'RES must cap results' requirement.

The result storage limit is stated twice and the copies disagree: SECURITY-SPEC calls it 'Proposed with RES-2, not yet confirmed by the human' while TECHNICAL-SPEC states it as settled, which breaks one home per fact and leaves the replaced 'RES must cap results' requirement ambiguous.

The result page's case title (in <title> and <h1>) and build label have no markup, direction-control or line-break display tests, and RES-2 has no RES-1.7-style criterion, although SECURITY-SPEC requires each slice to test the text its pages render.

The new Record result journey (radio outcome, Save draft, Submit, read-only view) has no Playwright end-to-end test, although builder.md requires browser tests for new UI journeys and src/e2e/test_tester.py was not extended.

The GET builds ResultForm with result_initial(existing) as submitted data, and an empty dict still counts as submitted, so a fresh record page shows "Choose Pass or Fail." before the tester enters anything.
No unit or e2e test checks that the fresh record page has no validation error, so the bound-form bug passes the suite.
The User Guide says opening a result page again after submission shows "This result has already been submitted.", but a GET shows the read-only result and only a POST gets that 409.
SECURITY-SPEC leaves an unaccepted open storage gap (results add ~17.9 GiB/day at the demo-creation cap, with no result write rate limit) that a human must accept or mitigate before merge.

SECURITY-SPEC replaces 'RES must cap results' with a per-workspace bound but omits the ~4.8 billion characters/day it allows at the 200-workspace daily cap (about 12x the accepted round residual) and leaves it 'open' instead of recording a decision or residual for the human.

RES-2.6 claims saves racing a retest are serialised, but only close races are tested, the security spec's 'submit racing a retest' test commitment was deleted rather than met, and a concurrent double submit is untested.

No test exercises the view's round lock: the close/retest tests commit before the POST so only the pre-lock check runs, and both race tests would still pass with select_for_update removed because the unique-index wait plus IntegrityError re-read gives the same 302/409, while the earlier spec promise of submit-racing-close/retest tests was dropped.

SECURITY-SPEC adds a per-round 1.2M-character results figure to a per-day 419M estimate, understating the daily increase by about 11 times (about 4.8 billion characters), and replaces 'RES must cap results' with a risk the agent accepted itself.

IPv4-mapped IPv6 REMOTE_ADDR values (::ffff:a.b.c.d) all normalise to ::/64, so every IPv4 client on a dual-stack server shares one counter, contrary to 'IPv4 addresses count individually' and enabling a global sign-in lockout.

The TECHNICAL-SPEC limit-counter note was rewritten to fit the implementation (on-demand insert, separate lock, 'unstarted' window) instead of building to the note as it stood ('inserted or updated in one statement'), without confirmation.

SECURITY-SPEC lists three new residual gaps as 'accepted' that no human accepted, and leaves a 'Not accepted, awaiting a human decision from the #4 review' paragraph instead of applying the smallest option and recording it in the report.

ACC-3.7's lock/statement-timeout path is never exercised end to end and the timeout test calls set_timeouts directly, so removing it from either view, or a failure while recording or committing, would go undetected.

TECHNICAL-SPEC says that after ACC-3 any accounts route that cannot reach storage gives the 503, but only the limit transactions do; /, GET /sign-in/, /coordinator/, /tester/, /demo/'s signed-in check and sign-in's post-commit session writes still give the generic 500 (rounds/tests/test_views.py:500 still asserts 500, and spec lines 55 and 84 were not reconciled).

Against the decision to build to the technical notes as they stand, the change adds an IPv4-mapped-IPv6 client-address rule and rewrites the counter-insert note in TECHNICAL-SPEC instead of raising them as decisions.

canonical_address groups IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (::ffff:a.b.c.d) into ::/64, so on a dual-stack listener every IPv4 client shares one sign-in and demo counter, contrary to 'IPv4 addresses count individually'.

The new User Guide storage-failure line claims the start page, sign-in, sign-out and home pages all show the 503 and nothing changes, but a signed-out start page needs no storage, the accepted sign-out residual gives a 500 after ending the session, and a failed session save after sign-in gives a 400.

The accounts-routes rule still says any route that cannot reach storage gives the 503, but the rewritten delivery-order sentence narrows it to three places, and sign-in's post-transaction session writes, /tester/ and / still give the generic 500.

TECHNICAL-SPEC requirement text was rewritten without human confirmation (sign-out storage exception widened to any failure, new logging rule, new IPv4-mapped rule), against the decision to build to the specs as they stand.

A storage failure while starting the session after a correct sign-in gives the generic 500 instead of the required 503, and the candidate rewrote TECHNICAL-SPEC to allow it, although SessionMiddleware already saves nothing for any status of 500 or above, so a 503 would be equally safe.

The new sign-in exception in TECHNICAL-SPEC 'Accounts routes' changes the confirmed requirement instead of being raised, which makes the User Guide's storage-failure sentence for the sign-in page inaccurate on the success path.

The changed technical spec says ACC-3 makes every accounts-route storage failure give the 503, but sign-in's session writes (cycle_key/login), sign-in GET and the role homes still give the 500, and an existing test (rounds/tests/test_views.py:500) still asserts that 500.
ACC-3.1 requires a 429 sign-in page, but the view renders the generic 429.html (titled Relay, no sign-in form), and the tests check only the status and message.

The technical note says per-address rows are inserted or updated in one statement, but _locked_row uses get_or_create plus a separate SELECT FOR UPDATE, so code and spec disagree and the race on a row's first insert is untested.

The ACC-3 technical notes were rewritten to fit the implementation (the one-statement insert-or-update replaced by insert-if-absent, select-for-update and update; a new IPv4-mapped rule; a new claim about timeout verification) instead of being built to as they stood, with no human decision.

Per-address counter rows are created and updated with get_or_create plus select_for_update plus save, not 'inserted or updated in one statement' as the unchanged TECHNICAL-SPEC limit-counter note requires.
ACC-3.7's lock/statement-timeout path is never exercised; storage failure is only simulated by mocking select_for_update, and the timeouts are only checked via SHOW.

unavailable_on_storage_failure turns storage errors on /, sign-in GET, /coordinator/, /tester/ and /demo/'s signed-in check into 503, beyond ACC-3.7 and TECHNICAL-SPEC's Data model rule that such routes keep their existing error page (generic 500), and the existing rounds test asserting 500 was flipped.

The candidate rewrote TECHNICAL-SPEC's delivery-order sentence to make every accounts route give the 503 with an unexplained sign-out exception, changing the spec rather than building to it as it stood and leaving it inconsistent with the Data model storage-exhaustion note.

opus_cost_split.note: Fitted to Claude Code's reported costs, not published prices.
